# OFFICIAL EVIDENCE — KTH Master's Programme in Computer Science (entry requirements)

**Source URL:** https://www.kth.se/en/studies/master/computer-science/entry-requirements-computer-science-1.419975

Note: The page addresses the *admission/entry requirements* page. It does not itself carry a stated application-cycle year; it references the admission process and a 2026 acceptance-rate statistic. Fall-2027 cycle specifics (e.g., exact deadlines, applicable year) are not stated on this page and remain unknown from this source. All figures below are as stated verbatim on this page.

---

## 1. General admission process
- To be admitted to the master's programme in Computer Science, you must meet the admission requirements, submit all application documents, and pass the selection.
- The same process applies to students with a bachelor's degree from a Swedish university.

---

## 2. Admission requirements — Bachelor's degree
- Academic qualifications from an internationally recognised university **equivalent to a Swedish bachelor's degree**.
- **Final-year condition:** You can meet the requirement if you are in the final year of your bachelor's studies.
  - Students at universities **abroad** must submit documents according to the instructions from University Admissions.
  - Students at **Swedish universities** must have completed **150 credits in their programme by 1 February** per the instructions from KTH.

---

## 3. Admission requirements — English proficiency
- English proficiency equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course **English 6 / English Level 2**.
- You can meet the requirement with an English test, **for example an overall IELTS score of 6.5 or a TOEFL score of 4.5**.
- Depending on your country of previous studies, you could also meet the requirement through completed upper secondary or university studies.
- The page refers to University Admissions to see all recognised English tests and what applies to your country of previous studies.

---

## 4. Specific requirements for Computer Science
A bachelor's degree corresponding to **180 ECTS credits, or equivalent**, including courses in:

**Mathematics:** four different subjects with a total of **28.5 ECTS credits**. These subjects must include:
- a course in **Calculus in one variable**,
- a course in **Linear Algebra**,
- a course in **Probability Theory and Statistics**,
- a course in **Discrete Mathematics**.

**Computer technology / Computer science and engineering / Computer science / Information technology:** three different subjects with a total of **22.5 ECTS credits**. These subjects must include:
- a course in **Object Oriented Programming**,
- a course in **Algorithms and Data Structures**,
- an **in-depth course in Algorithmic Complexity**.

---

## 5. Track / specialisation applicability (pre-enrolment vs in-program rules)
- Within the programme track, there may be courses with **additional requirements for special qualifications**. The requirements are stated under the heading **"Special eligibility"** in the syllabus. Examples given:
  - **Multivariable analysis** is a special eligibility requirement for compulsory courses within the tracks **Data analysis** and **Cognitive systems**.
  - **Human-computer interaction** is a special entry requirement for compulsory courses within the **Interaction Design** track.
  - **Additional prerequisites may exist** for some conditionally elective or recommended courses within the tracks.

---

## 6. Application documents (general instructions)
- You need to submit all of the following documents according to the instructions from University Admissions.
- Do **not submit documents that are not requested**.

**General document — Degree certificates:**
- Official certificates of your completed degrees. Documentation requirements vary between countries (see University Admissions).

**General document — Transcript:**
- Official transcript of courses and grades completed in your degree.
- Students from Swedish universities that use **Ladok** do not need to submit degree certificates or transcripts.

**General document — Proof of English proficiency:**
- What proof you need depends on whether you meet the requirement through a test or previous studies.

**General document — Identification:**
- A copy of passport with personal data and photograph, or other identification document.

---

## 7. Programme document — CV
- KTH does not require a standard template.
- The CV should clearly and concisely outline: education, relevant research or work experience, extracurricular activities, qualifications and achievements (awards, publications, expertise knowledge and skills, etc.).
- **Must be written in English.**

---

## 8. Programme document — Letter of motivation (constraints)
- Explains why you chose this programme at KTH, what you hope to gain from it, and how your interests and skills will help you succeed.
- Include an **autobiography** with the development and relevance of your academic and professional pursuits, extra-curricular activities and related experiences.
- KTH does not require a standard template.
- **Must be in English and less than 500 words.**
- If you apply to multiple programmes that require a letter of motivation, you should submit **one for each** and **state which programme each letter applies to at the top of the page**.

---

## 9. Programme document — Letters of recommendation (submission rules)
- **Two letters of recommendation** describing why you are the right choice for admission.
- Preferably, have **one referee from an academic environment and one from a professional setting**.
- If you apply for multiple programmes at KTH that request letters of recommendation, **you may use the same letters for several programmes**.
- You must provide an **English translation if the letters are in a different language**.
- The letters must have the referees' **full contact details**.
- **Referee submission rule:** If your referee wants to submit the letter themselves, they must send it **by post to University Admissions** and state your name and application number. **They cannot submit the letter via email.**

---

## 10. Summary sheet (submission rule)
- Submit the **summary sheet for Computer Science via the link when the application opens** — **do not upload it to your application on universityadmissions.se**.
- If you do **not submit a complete summary sheet, it will negatively affect your evaluation score**.
- Fill out all required information before submitting the form.
- For questions, contact the programme coordinator directly.

---

## 11. Selection criteria
- Based on the following criteria:
  - **study results** (grades from previous studies),
  - **motivation for the studies** (awards, prizes and publications),
  - **previous education**.
- **Prior education** is evaluated based on the quality and suitability of the subjects that are relevant for the programme applied to.
- For **international prior education, university ranking is also part of the merit rating**.
- The merit rating is carried out on a **scale of 1–75**.

---

## 12. Acceptance rate (as stated on the page)
- The acceptance rate for the master's programme in Computer Science **for 2026 was 8%**.
- KTH admitted **63 students out of the 762 applicants who met the admission requirements**.
- KTH advises applying to more than one programme to increase chances. You can apply for **up to four programmes** and rank them in your order of preference.

---

## 13. Recognition of prior learning
- If you entirely or partially lack a formal requirement for a course or programme but believe you have the necessary knowledge to meet it, you can apply for **recognition of prior learning**.

---

# OFFICIAL EVIDENCE — KTH Master's Programme in Computer Science (entry requirements)

**Source URL:** https://www.kth.se/en/studies/master/computer-science/entry-requirements-computer-science-1.419975

---

## 1. General admission process
- To be admitted to the master's programme in Computer Science, you must meet the admission requirements, submit all application documents, and pass the selection.
- The same process applies to students with a bachelor's degree from a Swedish university.

---

## 2. Admission requirements — Bachelor's degree
- Academic qualifications from an internationally recognised university **equivalent to a Swedish bachelor's degree**.
- **Final-year condition:** You can meet the requirement if you are in the final year of your bachelor's studies.
  - Students at universities **abroad** must submit documents according to the instructions from University Admissions.
  - Students at **Swedish universities** must have completed **150 credits in their programme by 1 February** per the instructions from KTH.

---

## 3. Admission requirements — English proficiency
- English proficiency equivalent to the Swedish upper secondary course **English 6 / English Level 2**.
- You can meet the requirement with an English test, **for example an overall IELTS score of 6.5 or a TOEFL score of 4.5**.
- Depending on your country of previous studies, you could also meet the requirement through completed upper secondary or university studies.
- The page refers to University Admissions to see all recognised English tests and what applies to your country of previous studies.

---

## 4. Specific requirements for Computer Science
A bachelor's degree corresponding to **180 ECTS credits, or equivalent**, including courses in:

**Mathematics:** four different subjects with a total of **28.5 ECTS credits**. These subjects must include:
- a course in **Calculus in one variable**,
- a course in **Linear Algebra**,
- a course in **Probability Theory and Statistics**,
- a course in **Discrete Mathematics**.

**Computer technology / Computer science and engineering / Computer science / Information technology:** three different subjects with a total of **22.5 ECTS credits**. These subjects must include:
- a course in **Object Oriented Programming**,
- a course in **Algorithms and Data Structures**,
- an **in-depth course in Algorithmic Complexity**.

---

## 5. Track / specialisation applicability (pre-enrolment vs in-program rules)
- Within the programme track, there may be courses with **additional requirements for special qualifications**. The requirements are stated under the heading **"Special eligibility"** in the syllabus. Examples given:
  - **Multivariable analysis** is a special eligibility requirement for compulsory courses within the tracks **Data analysis** and **Cognitive systems**.
  - **Human-computer interaction** is a special entry requirement for compulsory courses within the **Interaction Design** track.
  - **Additional prerequisites may exist** for some conditionally elective or recommended courses within the tracks.

---

## 6. Application documents (general instructions)
- You need to submit all of the following documents according to the instructions from University Admissions.
- Do **not submit documents that are not requested**.

**General document — Degree certificates:**
- Official certificates of your completed degrees. Documentation requirements vary between countries (see University Admissions).

**General document — Transcript:**
- Official transcript of courses and grades completed in your degree.
- Students from Swedish universities that use **Ladok** do not need to submit degree certificates or transcripts.

**General document — Proof of English proficiency:**
- What proof you need depends on whether you meet the requirement through a test or previous studies.

**General document — Identification:**
- A copy of passport with personal data and photograph, or other identification document.

---

## 7. Programme document — CV
- KTH does not require a standard template.
- The CV should clearly and concisely outline: education, relevant research or work experience, extracurricular activities, qualifications and achievements (awards, publications, expertise knowledge and skills, etc.).
- **Must be written in English.**

---

## 8. Programme document — Letter of motivation (constraints)
- Explains why you chose this programme at KTH, what you hope to gain from it, and how your interests and skills will help you succeed.
- Include an **autobiography** with the development and relevance of your academic and professional pursuits, extra-curricular activities and related experiences.
- KTH does not require a standard template.
- **Must be in English and less than 500 words.**
- If you apply to multiple programmes that require a letter of motivation, you should submit **one for each** and **state which programme each letter applies to at the top of the page**.

---

## 9. Programme document — Letters of recommendation (submission rules)
- **Two letters of recommendation** describing why you are the right choice for admission.
- Preferably, have **one referee from an academic environment and one from a professional setting**.
- If you apply for multiple programmes at KTH that request letters of recommendation, **you may use the same letters for several programmes**.
- You must provide an **English translation if the letters are in a different language**.
- The letters must have the referees' **full contact details**.
- **Referee submission rule:** If your referee wants to submit the letter themselves, they must send it **by post to University Admissions** and state your name and application number. **They cannot submit the letter via email.**

---

## 10. Summary sheet (submission rule)
- Submit the **summary sheet for Computer Science via the link when the application opens** — **do not upload it to your application on universityadmissions.se**.
- If you do **not submit a complete summary sheet, it will negatively affect your evaluation score**.
- Fill out all required information before submitting the form.
- For questions, contact the programme coordinator directly.

---

## 11. Selection criteria
- Based on the following criteria:
  - **study results** (grades from previous studies),
  - **motivation for the studies** (awards, prizes and publications),
  - **previous education**.
- **Prior education** is evaluated based on the quality and suitability of the subjects that are relevant for the programme applied to.
- For **international prior education, university ranking is also part of the merit rating**.
- The merit rating is carried out on a **scale of 1–75**.

---

## 12. Acceptance rate (as stated on the page)
- The acceptance rate for the master's programme in Computer Science **for 2026 was 8%**.
- KTH admitted **63 students out of the 762 applicants who met the admission requirements**.
- KTH advises applying to more than one programme to increase chances. You can apply for **up to four programmes** and rank them in your order of preference.

---

## 13. Recognition of prior learning
- If you entirely or partially lack a formal requirement for a course or programme but believe you have the necessary knowledge to meet it, you can apply for **recognition of prior learning**.
